# Writing Outline Builder

## When to Use
- You have scattered ideas and need a coherent structure.
- You want to turn research into an article readers can follow.
- You need a section plan before drafting or rewriting.

## Inputs
- Draft path or source notes.
- Optional target length and tone.
- Optional must-include examples or anecdotes.

## Procedure
1. Read the source draft or notes and extract the core thesis.
2. Identify the reader promise and the strongest supporting evidence.
3. Group ideas into 3 to 5 main sections.
4. Sequence sections for momentum: hook, insight buildup, payoff.
5. For each section, define purpose, key claim, proof, and transition.
6. Build the final outline with [outline template](./assets/outline-template.md).
7. Add optional title candidates and a closing takeaway.

## Quarto Alignment
- Keep structure compatible with post-style markdown and headings.
- Reflect frontmatter intent such as title, description, and categories.
- If the source is a draft post, preserve what already works.

## Output Contract
- One complete outline with intro, body sections, and conclusion.
- Section-level bullets for claim, evidence, and transition.
- Optional hooks and title ideas if requested.

## Guardrails
- Avoid section bloat; each section needs a clear purpose.
- Do not force symmetry if the argument needs uneven sections.
- Preserve author voice and practical clarity.
